content.title: About
content.content: A low‑fat bran with fruit muffin is a baked snack enriched with whole wheat bran and pieces of dried fruit. With a modest fat content (2600 kcal per 100 g) it fits well into diet plans, while the natural fruit sweetness provides flavor without added sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bran is a rich source of dietary fiber that supports regular bowel movements.
Dried fruit retains most of the vitamins and minerals found in fresh fruit.
Low‑fat recipes often replace butter with applesauce or yogurt, lowering calories while keeping moisture.
Muffins are easy to portion into individual packs, making them popular in school cafeterias and office snack boxes.
When stored properly, the muffin stays fresh for up to 5 days.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Bran provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, which aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Reduced fat helps control overall calorie intake, beneficial for weight management.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from fruit
items.content: Dried fruit adds vitamin C, potassium and iron, supporting immune function and energy metabolism.

items.title: Stable blood‑sugar release
items.content: Complex carbohydrates from bran release glucose slowly, preventing rapid blood‑sugar spikes.

items.title: Supports gut microbiota
items.content: Fiber acts as a prebiotic, fostering growth of beneficial intestinal bacteria.

items.title: Wheat/gluten allergy
items.content: Bran contains gluten, so the product is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar from dried fruit
items.content: Although low‑fat, the natural sugars in dried fruit may affect blood‑sugar levels, which diabetics should monitor.

items.title: Excessive fiber intake
items.content: Very high fiber consumption can cause bloating and gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Preservatives in commercial versions
items.content: Some factory‑made muffins may contain additives for longer shelf life; always check the ingredient list.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The muffin can be enjoyed as a quick snack, sliced and paired with low‑fat yogurt, cottage cheese, or nut butter. It also works well crumbled over salads, as a base for dessert parfaits, or simply taken on the go.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the muffin in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer freshness keep it refrigerated – up to 7 days – or freeze individual portions, where it retains quality for about 3 months. Discard if you notice mold or off‑odors.
